Recommendation: Fix the data foundation before further modelling
Evidence: Only 5,000 of 60,000 billed appointments exist in the Appointments table; 95% of appointments point to a department owned by another facility; no facility master, bed status or equipment availability fields.
Strength of evidence: High — verified by direct key checks
Suggested action: Re-extract Appointments for the full year; enforce Facility→Department→Doctor foreign keys; add Facility master, bed status and equipment condition fields.

Recommendation: Stop using bill 'Status' as a collections indicator
Evidence: 80% of bills are paid in full whatever Status says; 'Pending' bills have the same average payment ratio (90%) as 'Paid'.
Suggested action: Derive Status from Amount vs AmountPaid in the billing system; reconcile Revenue_Summary (1.13 bn) with billing (9.31 bn).

Recommendation: Target outreach with a rule-based list, not a predictive model
Evidence: 6,662 patients (33.3%) meet the high-risk rule (65+/50–64 with chronic disease, obesity or underweight); only 1,498 had an appointment in 2026. Chronic disease affects 74.6% of patients but no demographic factor predicts it (AUC 0.51).
Strength of evidence: Medium — rule is clinical logic; data cannot validate it
Suggested action: Call-back / screening programme for the high-risk list, prioritising patients aged 65+ with a chronic condition and no 2026 visit; evaluate uptake to validate the rule.

Recommendation: Redesign the feedback instrument and capture real drivers
Evidence: Mean rating 2.99/5; 40% rate 1–2. Ratings are unrelated to comment text, diagnosis, billing, department, facility or any modelled variable (best R² ≈ 0).
Strength of evidence: High (that data cannot explain satisfaction); drivers unknown
Suggested action: Add wait time, staff courtesy, cleanliness, drug availability and discharge-time questions; validate comment/rating consistency; collect ≥ 348 ratings per facility to detect a 0.3-point difference with 80% power (currently ≈ 89).

Recommendation: Do not rank facilities or departments on current ratings
Evidence: Facility means 2.76–3.19, department means 2.76–3.02; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.80 (facilities), 0.88 (departments).
Suggested action: Publish confidence intervals with any league table; investigate the lowest-rated sites only after the new instrument yields adequate samples.

Evidence: Facility volumes range 217–278 (28% spread) while headcount is 61–64 everywhere; staff numbers do not track volume (ρ = -0.10). Doctor load is random (variance/mean 0.95), i.e. nobody is systematically overloaded.
Strength of evidence: Medium — the volume gap is not statistically significant (p = 0.052) but is practically large
Suggested action: Move toward a staffing ratio per 1,000 appointments; rebalance rotas from the quietest sites toward HF013/HF011 as a pilot; review monthly with a rolling 3-month workload index.

Recommendation: Verify bed capacity before any bed-related investment
Evidence: All 2,000 beds are flagged 'Available'; recorded admissions imply only ≈3.8% annual bed-day use.
Strength of evidence: Low — Admissions table appears to be an extract
Suggested action: Capture daily bed census; if the 4% figure holds, consolidate wards rather than expand.

Evidence: Lab test type is unrelated to diagnosis (χ² p = 0.366) — e.g. malaria patients are not more likely to get a malaria test — while prescribing matches diagnosis 100%.
Strength of evidence: Medium — may be a data-linkage artefact
Suggested action: Audit test-ordering against diagnostic protocols; link lab orders to diagnosis codes.

Recommendation: Collect the outstanding balance and clear pending claims
Evidence: 0.92 bn RWF (9.9%) of billed amounts is unpaid; 21,028 claims worth 2.44 bn RWF are 'Pending' and only 50% of claims are approved (no difference by provider, p = 0.08).
Suggested action: Weekly ageing report on outstanding balances; dedicated follow-up team for pending claims; agree turnaround SLAs with all four insurers; 0.64 bn RWF of 'Insurance'-method payments have no claim on file — reconcile.

Recommendation: Budget on a flat baseline and manage volatility
Evidence: 2027 forecast ≈ 1.10 bn RWF (92 M/month, 95% band ±68%); no trend is detectable (12 months cannot reveal seasonality), and revenue is only weakly tied to visit counts (r = 0.28).
Suggested action: Set the budget at the forecast mean with a contingency reserve; analyse the Sep-2026 peak (146 M) and Dec-2026 trough (67 M) for one-off billing events; collect 24+ months before using seasonal models.

Recommendation: Do not expand on current evidence — build the evidence
Evidence: Demand is flat (no trend, ρ = -0.14), evenly spread across provinces (19.6%–20.5%) and departments; admissions cannot be predicted; facility locations and service-level data are missing.
Suggested action: Add facility geography (district, ownership, type) and ServiceID on bills; re-run province-level demand vs capacity once available. Prioritise Cardiology and Radiology for a staffing review (highest forecast load index, ≈105–109), but treat as provisional.
